**3B.4 Research Note**

Bottom line: I found no credible 2024 evidence that Hasina built effective due-process, complaint-handling, civilian-oversight, or independent-investigation systems for abuse by police, military, intelligence, prisons, or Awami League-linked actors. The record is dominated by coercive shutdowns, impunity, and later external fact-finding rather than domestic accountability.

- [Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024. Claim: Reuters described a nationwide curfew and internet/text shutdown as the state escalated against protesters; that is the opposite of transparent complaint handling or civilian oversight and suggests suppression of scrutiny. IDs: `3B.4`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`
- [Bangladesh’s crackdown on protesters left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024. Claim: The UN said the crackdown left more than 170 dead and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity; this is strong evidence against any functioning system for independent investigation or restraint of abusive actors. IDs: `3B.4`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh back UN investigation of grave abuses](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses) — Human Rights Watch, August 26, 2024. Claim: HRW said the crackdown was the deadliest in recent Bangladeshi history, with excessive force by law enforcement and Awami League-affiliated youth violence; the report implies the state did not prevent or punish abuse by politically protected actors. IDs: `3B.4`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.5`, `2B.9`
- [Former Bangladesh PM Hasina demands probe into July "killings and vandalism"](https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/) — Reuters, August 13, 2024. Claim: After fleeing, Hasina called for an investigation into the killings and vandalism; this is the closest pro-accountability signal, but it is post-hoc and does not show she had built or used an effective accountability system while in power. IDs: `3B.4`, `2B.9`
- [UN fact-finding team issues call for submissions](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/278741-un-fact-finding-team-issues-call-submissions) — United Nations in Bangladesh / OHCHR, September 16, 2024. Claim: The UN opened a fact-finding process for alleged violations from July 1 to August 15, 2024; this indicates outside investigators had to step in rather than any credible domestic mechanism resolving abuse. IDs: `3B.4`, `3B.2`, `2B.9`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find reliable 2024 reporting showing Hasina created independent complaint channels, empowered civilian oversight bodies, or ordered genuinely independent investigations into abuse by police, military, or Awami League-aligned enforcers.
- I also did not find credible evidence that politically protected actors were meaningfully disciplined through domestic processes in 2024.
- The only counterevidence is her post-fleeing call for an investigation, which is too late and too narrow to count as building a system.
